title: Bookmarked: News Stories On Our Reading List
summary: Bigfoot leaves a paper-trail, the gas prices in GTA VI, splitting the Bloomin Onion bill on a date, the board games people cheat at the most, and evidence of cheating on our very show: Join hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo on Bloomberg This Weekend for Bookmarked, where they share stories that caught their attention over the past week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
summary: A gift of GTA VI coming with a contract, what that SNL ‘Sister’ sketch says about American healthcare, Robert Pattinson as Bond, and the F1 aspirations of children: Join Lisa Mateo, David Gura and Christina Ruffini for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rahm Emanuel Says Trump Is Playing Into China’s Hands
summary: Former US Ambassador to Japan Rahm Emanuel tells Bloomberg This Weekend that he is seriously considering a 2028 presidential run as he lays out an economic vision focused on reforming capitalism, combating corruption and strengthening the middle class. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Emanuel also criticizes President Donald Trump’s approach to China and Russia, arguing that the US should work more closely with allies to counter Beijing and protect American economic and national security interests.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Yardeni Cuts S&P 500 Target Again, Says Bear Market Is Unlikely
summary: Wall Street strategist Ed Yardeni cut his S&P 500 Index year-end forecast for the second time in about two months in the wake of a powerful stock selloff that pushed the benchmark into a technical correction.

title: Investors Brave Stock Market ‘Fragility’ as AI Trade Falters
summary: The stomach-churning selloff that rocked equities has options traders girding for more volatility ahead.

title: Storm Devastates Rural Brazilian Town in Threat to Crops, Lives
summary: A heavy storm that hit Brazil’s southern state of Rio Grande do Sul on Friday devastated a small town and raised concerns that continued rains and strong winds may bring further damage to crucial agriculture areas.

title: GTA VI Takes Over Thanksgiving Week
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg reporter Josyana Joshua tells host Lisa Mateo how the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI is becoming a cultural and workplace phenomenon, with gamers taking time off and preparing to play through Thanksgiving week. Joshua explains how the game’s 13-year buildup is driving demand for consoles and gaming gear while potentially competing with family gatherings, football and other holiday entertainment. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Fed’s Inflation Fight May Require More Hikes
summary: Neil Dutta, head of US economic research at Renaissance Macro Research, tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Federal Reserve made a mistake by holding rates steady in October and may need multiple hikes as inflation remains stubbornly above its 2% target. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Dutta says the recent market selloff does not yet signal broader economic trouble, arguing that AI investment and a resilient labor market continue to support growth even as the Fed has less flexibility to cushion falling markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Governors Push States to Lead on AI
summary: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Governors Wes Moore, Spencer Cox, Josh Stein and Mike Braun tell host Christina Ruffini that states need to take a larger role in shaping AI and data center policy as concerns grow over electricity costs, water use, jobs and consumer protections. The bipartisan group says data centers should largely pay for their own energy needs and emphasizes local control, while differing over how aggressively the federal government should regulate AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Strong Earnings Prove No Match for the Crumbling AI Trade
summary: For years, a strong earnings season has given Wall Street something to fall back on. But the crumbling artificial-intelligence trade has ripped away that support.

title: Oil Shock Response Sets Emerging-Market Bond Winners and Losers
summary: Fuel subsidies are driving a widening divide in emerging markets, with investors favoring bonds from nations that have taken the painful steps to curb them.

title: Why Your Health Insurance Keeps Getting More Expensive
summary: The average employer-sponsored family health plan now costs more than $28,000 a year, about the price of a new car, and premiums are expected to climb even faster in 2027. As costs rise, more of the bill is coming out of workers’ paychecks, and health care has become a top budget concern for CFOs.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: S. Korea Rolls Out Phased Measures to Stabilize Stock Market
summary: South Korea announced phased measures to calm markets amid rising volatility, including ensuring a stock stabilization fund is in place to respond when needed, top financial officials said after an emergency meeting on Sunday.

title: Trump’s Asia Trip Leaves Key Issues Unresolved
summary: ABC News State Department reporter Shannon Kingston tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia’s increasingly provocative actions near NATO countries are complicating President Donald Trump’s push for a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, while Moscow remains publicly defiant. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kingston says Trump’s Asia trip produced few concrete results and puts greater pressure on the upcoming G20 meetings to deliver progress on China, trade and other unresolved diplomatic issues. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Taiwan Mulls Lowering Margin Requirement to Support Stock Market
summary: Taiwan is considering lowering the margin requirement ratio for stock investors using borrowed funds as it tries to stem a selloff after the benchmark equity index’s worst week in 35 years.

title: Asia’s Stock Rescue Efforts Gather Pace After Wall Street Plunge
summary: Asian authorities are stepping up efforts to stem a deepening stock-market rout, with China easing margin requirements, and Taiwan and South Korea rolling out intervention measures following Friday’s plunge in US equities.

title: From Squeezes to Meltdown, a Week of Mayhem Rocks Metals Markets
summary: As the copper industry gathered in Shanghai last week, Grace Li was struck by the overwhelmingly bearish mood over the outlook for demand. She agreed with the pessimism. In fact, she came close to pulling out her phone on the spot to put on a short position after her Monday conversations.

title: China’s $1.7 Trillion AI Rout Turns Hot Trade Into Losing Bet
summary: China’s AI stock trade, once a hot bet as the nation’s technology powerhouses raced to catch up with the US, has morphed into a losing strategy.

title: Russian Cargo Ship Attacked by Drones in Gulf of Finland
summary: Russia said a cargo ship bound for its Kaliningrad exclave was targeted in international waters in the Gulf of Finland, highlighting growing risks to the country’s energy and food exports through critical Baltic Sea shipping routes.
